sections.where: Prep notes · Book 4 Geography › D-2 › India - soil types, characteristics and distribution; soil erosion and conservation › Soil types → formation, parent rock, characteristics and regions
bullets: Red and yellow: Formation / parent material Crystalline igneous rocks (granite, gneiss) under low rainfall; Key traits Red from iron oxide, yellow when hydrated ; 5.18 lakh sq km; Main regions Kanyakumari-Jhansi, Kutch-Rajmahal (APP)
Arid/desert: Formation / parent material Wind-laid sand, low rainfall; Key traits Sandy, saline, low humus and N; kankar lower down; Main regions W Rajasthan

Black (regur / black cotton): Area / share 5.47 lakh sq km, 16.6%; Origin and properties From basalt (Deccan Trap); clay >62%; high moisture retention; deep cracks, "self-ploughing"; neutral to alkaline; rich in Ca, K, Mg, poor in N, P, humus; Where Maharashtra, Gujarat, MP, W. AP, N. Karnataka; Crops Cotton, jowar, chillies, tobacco

Red and yellow: Area / share 5.18 lakh sq km; Origin and properties Red from iron oxide; porous, light; poor in lime, humus, phosphoric acid; low moisture retention; Where Kanyakumari-Jhansi, Kutch-Rajmahal; Crops Ragi, groundnut, tobacco

Peaty soils form where heavy rainfall and high humidity keep soil waterlogged and organic matter piles up (APP). (The OCR answer key of the APPSC-G1 2024 peaty-soil question reads "semi-arid climate with salinity", which describes saline soils. Follow the waterlogged-organic description.)

sections.where: Prep notes · Book 3 Economy › C-5 › Approaches and initiatives in AP agriculture - APCNF/ZBNF, horticulture, aquaculture, allied sectors › Kharif vs rabi area trends
bullets: Kharif: Food-grain area 2023-24 18.13 lakh ha; Food-grain area 2024-25 20.36 lakh ha; Paddy area 2024-25 14.04 lakh ha
The 2024-25 rise (+12.85% area) followed an 11.7% rainfall surplus, after a 16.5% deficit in 2023-24.

Kharif 2026 is a drought season: all 28 districts are in deficit (25 deficit, 3 large-deficit). By 19 Aug only 18.9 lakh ha was sown, about 61% of the normal 30.84 lakh ha. Groundnut was at 34% of normal, paddy 62%, maize 61%, pulses 70%, cotton 75% (CDCA Aug 2026).

sections.where: Prep notes · Book 3 Economy › C-3 › Agricultural inputs - seeds, fertilisers and the subsidy regime, pesticides, mechanisation, extension services › Fertiliser subsidy - highest-subsidy fertiliser, NBS, DBT, neem-coated urea, nano urea/DAP, consumption
bullets: The fertiliser subsidy is the second-largest subsidy after food (VIS 2026).
Neem-coated urea: 100% of domestic urea from 1 Sep 2015 and of imported urea from 1 Dec 2015. It slows nitrogen release and stops diversion to industry (CDI).
Not in your sources: the current ranking of the largest fertiliser-consuming states.
Soil Health Cards: 25.79 crore generated, cutting fertiliser use 8-10% and raising yields 5-6% (LENS, May 2026) (ES: 25.55 crore as of Nov 2025); issued free every two years; launched 2015 .
PM-PRANAM (approved 28 June 2023): States get 50% of subsidy saved by cutting chemical fertiliser use (IYB 2026).

sections.where: Prep notes · Book 3 Economy › C-3 › Indian agriculture - importance, land use classification, cropping seasons and cropping pattern › Cropping seasons - kharif, rabi, zaid
bullets: Kharif: Sowing June-July (SW monsoon onset); Harvest Sep-Oct (APP) / Oct-Nov (APPCA 2026); Crops Rice, maize, jowar, bajra, cotton, groundnut, soybean, jute, sugarcane
Zaid is the short, irrigation-dependent summer season between the rabi harvest and kharif sowing (the PYQ key). Rabi crops depend on western disturbances and irrigation.
APP also lists the sub-seasons Zaid Kharif (Aug-Sep sowing) and Zaid Rabi (Feb-Mar sowing).
Grown in both seasons: pulses (tur/arhar kharif, gram/chana rabi); rice in irrigated deltas - AP 2024-25 paddy area 14.04 lakh ha kharif + 6.93 lakh ha rabi (APSES 2024-25, 2nd AE).
Both-season crops: moong and urad, and groundnut ; millets are mainly kharif but some are grown in the southern rabi (LENSD May 2026).

Obesity and heart disease come from excess energy intake plus low physical activity. A sedentary lifestyle and energy-dense foods lead to degenerative diseases. Both statements were correct in the PYQ.
Main risk factors: unhealthy diet, physical inactivity, tobacco, alcohol, urbanisation, ageing (UPSC). 24% of women and 23% of men are overweight or obese (NFHS-5, 2019-21; ES 2025-26).

sections.topic: Supreme Court and High Court Judges
sections.where: Rocket Sheets · Indian Polity › #71 · Supreme Court and High Court Judges
bullets: Supreme Court Judges are governed under Part V, Chapter IV of the Constitution.
The Governor has no power to appoint High Court Judges.
A distinguished jurist is eligible for appointment as a Supreme Court Judge under Article 124(3)(c).
The President transfers High Court Judges on the advice of a collegium led by the Chief Justice of India.
Another Judge of the same High Court may exercise writ jurisdiction over the High Court Chief Justice’s administrative actions.

sections.where: Prep notes · Book 2 Polity, Society & IR › B-2 › High Courts and subordinate judiciary; judicial review, judicial activism, PIL and judicial overreach debate › High Court judges - appointment, transfer, resignation, removal instances, writ and supervisory powers, contempt
bullets: Under Art. 217, the President appoints after consulting the CJI and the Governor, and for puisne judges also the HC Chief Justice. Proposals start with the HC Chief Justice and the HC collegium (CJ + 2), then go to the SC collegium (CJI + 2 senior-most judges) (LENSD 12 Aug 2026).
The inquiry report on Yashwant Varma (formerly Allahabad HC) was to be tabled despite his resignation (LENSD 11 Jul 2026).

Contempt: Arts. 129 and 215 make the SC and HCs courts of record. The Contempt of Courts Act, 1971 followed the H.N. Sanyal Committee and defines civil contempt (wilful disobedience) and criminal contempt (scandalising or obstructing justice). Fair criticism and accurate reporting are exceptions (VIS 2026).
Art. 215: every HC is a court of record; punishes contempt of itself and subordinate courts (SC: Art. 129).

Appellate: primarily a court of appeal; second civil appeals on questions of law only; death sentences of Sessions Courts need HC confirmation (now under BNSS 2023, which replaced CrPC from 1 July 2024) .

sections.where: Prep notes · Book 2 Polity, Society & IR › B-2 › Governor - appointment, powers, discretionary powers, position and controversies (Article 200/201, Article 356 reports) › Appointment and office - Articles 153-158, same Governor for two states, qualifications, pleasure (B.P. Singhal)
bullets: Art. 155: appointed by the President by warrant under hand and seal. The Governor is neither directly nor indirectly elected.

The term is 5 years, but he continues until his successor enters office . So "quits office immediately after the term expires" is the wrong statement (APPSC-G1 2019). He resigns to the President, may be transferred, and may be reappointed.

In B.P. Singhal v. UoI (2010), the pleasure doctrine is not unfettered: a Governor cannot be removed arbitrarily or merely because the Centre's government changes, and removal is open to limited judicial review . No grounds for removal are stated in the Constitution.
Grounds for removal are not stated in the Constitution. The President may transfer a Governor, and a Governor may be reappointed (APP).

Art 200 reservation: mandatory for bills endangering the High Court's position (APP; IYB). The President has an absolute veto over reserved bills (APP). APPSC 2025 key: reservation is an example of central control over states.

bullets: Rayalaseema lies in the rain shadow of the Western Ghats and the Karnataka/Telangana highlands, so it gets little SW-monsoon rain (CDI). Anantapur is the lowest-rainfall district.

2026: a deficient year. The SW monsoon deficit reached 51.2% (1 Jun-25 Aug), with all 28 districts deficient. Causes: El Nino subsidence, and all seven low-pressure systems forming at the head of the Bay (CDCA Aug 2026).

bullets: New Industrial Policy announced 24 July 1991.

Automatic approval for up to 51% foreign equity in a list of high-priority, high-investment, high-technology industries (e.g. capital goods, entertainment electronics, food processing) - not all industries (APPSC-G1 2012); also for export trading companies.
Automatic approval for foreign technology agreements in high-priority industries; use of foreign brand names/trademarks permitted; Foreign Investment Promotion Board (FIPB) set up to speed approvals.
Mandatory convertibility clause (lenders converting loans to equity) was relaxed for term loans; APPSC-G2 2025 key: it applies only to term loans of less than 10 years - learn the key's wording.

Now: FDI up to 100% under the automatic route in most sectors, negative-list approach; FIPB abolished June 2017; approvals via FIF portal, integrated with National Single Window System since Aug 2022 (IYB 2026).

sections.where: Prep notes · Book 2 Polity, Society & IR › B-4 › Social stratification and mobility in India › Mobility through reservation, education, migration
bullets: Education: better education brings better jobs and higher social standing; the emerging class system allows upward mobility (APP).
Reservation: backward classes in the South (Self-Respect Movement of Periyar) demanded reservation in government jobs; reservation led to group mobility (APP).
Reservation has also broadened the urban middle class by bringing in backward classes and Dalits (APP).
Occupational mobility: e.g., Ezhavas of Kerala moved from toddy tapping into tailoring and cottage industries (APP).
Migration and urbanisation: city anonymity and caste-blind public spaces weaken caste identity, but migrants carry caste networks and prejudices into cities (APP).

bullets: NTR Bharosa Pension (earlier YSR Pension Kanuka): ₹4,000/month to old-age and widow pensioners, enhanced from ₹3,000 w.e.f. April 2024 (APSES 2024-25).
Jan 2026: monthly distribution automated with Aadhaar-based biometric authentication to remove ghost beneficiaries; AP tops up the central NSAP pension from its own funds (APPCA).
2019-24: Name YSR Pension Kanuka (CDI quiz); Monthly amount (old age / widow) Raised in steps to ₹3,000 (APSES)

Scale: 61.92 lakh beneficiaries; ₹2,693 crore released for 1 Sep 2026; ₹73,506 crore spent on pensions since June 2024 (TH, 31 Aug 2026; earlier 63.12 lakh in Dec 2025, the largest share BC at 28.32 lakh). sections.where: Prep notes · Book 2 Polity, Society & IR › B-6 › Important flagship programmes of the Central Government - social sector (health, education, nutrition, housing) › Code on Social Security 2020 - gig and platform workers, e-Shram, unorganised workers
bullets: It merges 9 laws (EPF, ESI, Maternity Benefit, Gratuity, Unorganised Workers' Social Security Act, etc.). The four Labour Codes came into force on 21 Nov 2025, with the 2026 Central Rules (CDI Block15).

It recognises gig workers, platform workers and aggregators in law for the first time. Aggregators pay 1-2% of annual turnover (capped at 5% of payouts) into a social security fund. A National Social Security Board recommends schemes (CDI; LENS Jul 2025). Maternity leave stays at 26 weeks; a creche is required at 50+ employees.

e-Shram (26 Aug 2021, MoLE): Aadhaar-verified National Database of Unorganised Workers; 12-digit UAN; age 16-59; excludes income-tax payers and EPFO/ESIC members. The 2024 One-Stop Solution joins up 15 schemes; 31.87 crore registered (LENSD, 26 Aug and 16 Aug 2026).

sections.where: Prep notes · Book 2 Polity, Society & IR › B-3 › Central Information Commission and State Information Commissions; CBI and its legal basis › Digital Personal Data Protection Act 2023 amendments to RTI
bullets: DPDP Act 2023 amended Section 8(1)(j) of the RTI Act to exempt personal information outright, removing the public-interest override . The Congress president said it "diluted the RTI Act's public interest clause" (TH, 31 Jan 2026).

Economic Survey 2025-26 called for a "re-examination" of the RTI Act. It suggested exempting confidential service records and draft policy discussions, and floated a possible "ministerial veto" (TH, 31 Jan 2026).

bullets: Art. 72 President: pardon incl. death sentence and court-martial .
Art. 161 Governor: cannot pardon a death sentence, but can commute/remit/suspend .
Shatrughan Chauhan v UOI (2014): inordinate, unexplained delay in deciding mercy petitions is a ground to commute death to life .
Also: solitary confinement before rejection is illegal; 14 days between rejection and execution .
Epuru Sudhakar v Govt of AP (2006): pardon/remission is open to limited judicial review .

sections.where: Prep notes · Book 4 Geography › D-4 › Transport in Andhra Pradesh - highways, railway network, ports (Visakhapatnam, Krishnapatnam, Gangavaram, Kakinada), airports › Railway tunnels and port rail links in AP - longest electrified tunnel
bullets: Cherlopalli-Rapuru tunnel (6.6 km), SPSR Nellore - India's longest electrified rail tunnel when opened (2019), on the Obulavaripalle-Venkatachalam line that links Krishnapatnam port to the Rayalaseema hinterland . Nationally it is now exceeded by USBRL's T-50 (IYB).

Port rail links: Ramayapatnam sits next to NH-16 and Thettu station; Kakinada Gateway includes its own rail line (Survey 2025-26). Gap: last-mile rail to Kopparthy, Orvakal and Krishnapatnam nodes is incomplete (CDI Block10).

bullets: Rail links carry cement, granite and minerals to Visakhapatnam, Gangavaram and Krishnapatnam. The last-mile rail links to industrial nodes such as Kopparthy and Orvakal are incomplete, so industry depends on road (CDI).
Guntakal-Ballari 3rd & 4th lines: Facts Rayalaseema to Karnataka and Goa, plus Krishnapatnam and Ramayapatnam ports; ₹1,264 crore, +16.22 MTPA, target 2028-29 (CCEA, Jul 2026)
Kottavalasa-Kirandul (KK): Facts Bailadila iron ore to Visakhapatnam port through Eastern Ghats tunnels
South Coast Railway, the 18th zone with its headquarters at Visakhapatnam, became operational on 1 Jun 2026 under the AP Reorganisation Act 2014.
Tribal roads (RCPLWE): 27 roads + 14 bridges (397 km) built in Srikakulam, Vizianagaram, Visakhapatnam and East Godavari (APSES).

sections.where: Prep notes · Book 2 Polity, Society & IR › B-2 › Challenges in local devolution - funds, functions, functionaries; parallel bodies and capacity gaps › Delays in local body elections and SEC autonomy
bullets: Art. 243K (243ZA for municipalities): SEC appointed by the Governor, removable only like a High Court judge; service conditions cannot be varied to the SEC's disadvantage (APPCA, Apr 2026) [GK for last point].
Before 1993 states postponed local polls at will; the SEC and the 5-year term with elections before expiry (or within 6 months of dissolution, Arts. 243E/243U) made local government permanent (APP).

AP Cabinet (18 Aug 2026): 34% BC reservation in rural and 33⅓% in urban local bodies; elections to be expedited to secure Central funds (₹12,150 crore at risk if not done by October); direct election of Mayors and municipal chairpersons (TH, 19 Aug 2026).

bullets: Reddys, Kammas, Velamas, Kapus rose as martial and agrarian castes; the Kayasthas were an administrative elite (CDI).
The Justice Party rested on intermediate castes (Kammas, Reddys, Naidus). Non-Brahmin mobilisation led to the Communal G.O. of 1921 (CDI).
AP today: the EWS Welfare Department clubs the Reddy, Kamma, Kapu, Brahmin, Kshatriya, Vysya and EBC corporations; EWS pensions rose to ₹4,000 (APSES 2024-25 pp.261-262).

sections.where: Rocket Sheets · Indian Polity › #76 · Women’s Political Representation and Reservation
bullets: Women's political reservation was first constitutionally institutionalized through the 73rd and 74th Constitutional Amendment Acts, 1992.
Women's reservation in the House of the People covers seats reserved for Scheduled Castes and Scheduled Tribes.
Women's reservation in the Legislative Assembly of the National Capital Territory of Delhi covers Scheduled Caste-reserved seats.
Not less than one-third of the total seats reserved for Scheduled Castes and Scheduled Tribes under Article 243D(2) must be reserved for women belonging to Scheduled Castes and Scheduled Tribes.
The mandatory sub-quota for Scheduled Caste and Scheduled Tribe women within Scheduled Caste and Scheduled Tribe reserved seats is one-third.

bullets: Dumont: hierarchy rests on the pure vs impure; *Homo Hierarchicus* vs *Homo Aequalis* (CDX).
McKim Marriott: the interactional approach, ranking castes by exchange of "coded substances" (food, water, services) (CDX).
Traits: commensal taboos, the pollution-by-touch idea, untouchability, Sanskritic rituals (CDX, APP).
Dipankar Gupta counters Dumont: castes are discrete communities and "difference" is not "hierarchy" (CDX).

sections.topic: Seventh Schedule funds and power sharing
sections.where: Prep notes · Book 3 Economy › C-5 › Division of assets, liabilities, employees and institutions; Ninth and Tenth Schedule institutions › Seventh Schedule funds and power sharing - fund category, electricity allocation formula
bullets: The Seventh Schedule of the Act is the "List of Funds" in the Public Account, including provident, pension and insurance funds (APPSC 2022). Securities held against these funds are divided by population ratio (Sec 52).

Electricity (Twelfth Schedule): power from Central Generating Stations is shared on the actual consumption of the DISCOMs over the last 5 years. APGENCO plants go by location, and existing PPAs continue.
AP says this gave it about 46% of the power for 58% of the population (CDI Block13).

The APPSC-GS 2019 key marked "Gadgil formula" for the "electricity distribution formula" question. The Act's rule is the 5-year consumption basis. If the options force a choice, the key's answer is Gadgil.
A deficit State has first right of refusal on the other State's surplus power for 10 years.
